finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the POST /hooks/test handler passes a user-supplied callback URL straight to axios.post with no scheme, host, or IP validation. An attacker can make the server send requests to internal services, localhost, or cloud metadata endpoints such as 169.254.169.254. The response status is returned to the caller, which gives a port and host probing oracle. axios follows redirects by default, so redirect-based bypasses are also possible.

trace.note: Handler is registered on the `pub` router. No auth middleware is applied to it.
req.body.callback is passed unvalidated as the URL to axios.post.
The upstream status code is returned to the attacker.

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, no URL parsing, no scheme or host check, no private-IP or DNS-rebinding protection, and no redirect restriction. The `pub` router is not covered by requireAdmin. Whether `pub` has authentication when mounted cannot be seen, because only routes.js is present.

verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 registers POST /hooks/test on `pub` with no auth middleware (requireAdmin at routes.js:12 is applied only to `admin`), and routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback unvalidated to axios.post and returns the status at line 21; mount-time auth is not visible, but nothing in the file guards the route.

finding.claim: SSRF in the admin diagnostics fetch endpoint. The query parameter `url` is passed unvalidated to axios.get, so an admin, or anyone who hijacks an admin session, can reach internal hosts and metadata services. The response status is returned. This is lower severity because it is restricted to admins, but there is no destination validation.

trace.note: req.query.url is passed unvalidated to axios.get.
The upstream status code is returned to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) requires session.role === 'admin'. This limits who can reach the sink but does not constrain the destination. There is no URL allowlist, no private-IP blocking, and no redirect control. Whether the admin router is actually mounted cannot be seen, because only routes.js is present.

verdict.guard_found: none on the destination; only the requireAdmin role check (routes.js:7-12), which gates who can call the endpoint
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12, 15, 16) and no destination guard exists, but the sink at routes.js:15 is only reachable through admin.use(requireAdmin) at routes.js:12, which returns 403 unless session.role is "admin" (routes.js:8). So an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot control `url`. The separate unauthenticated pub.post("/hooks/test") callback at routes.js:20 is a different finding.
